findings.title: ClientCredentialsGrantType never records its grant type, so client_credentials access tokens are encoded with the UNKNOWN shortcut "na" instead of "cc"
findings.description:
`process` builds its token directly with `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` (lines 140-141) rather than through `createTokenResponse`. The `setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, ...)` added in `OAuth2GrantTypeBase.createTokenResponse` (OAuth2GrantTypeBase.java:109) therefore never runs. The path continues through `generateAccessToken()` → `createClientAccessToken` (TokenManager.java:1203-1205, 611-613) → `initToken` (TokenManager.java:1052-1054). There, `getTokenContextFromClientSessionContext` reads the attribute as null and substitutes `UNKNOWN` ("na", DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:57-60). A transient client-credentials token is therefore issued with an ID like `trrtna:<uuid>`, not `trrtcc:<uuid>`, even though `ClientCredentialsGrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()` returns "cc". The `testSuccessClientCredentialsToken` unit test uses `trltcc` as its sample, which shows the intended value, but it only exercises the encoder and no test covers this real path.

Fix: call `clientSessionCtx.setAttribute(Constants.GRANT_TYPE, OAuth2Constants.CLIENT_CREDENTIALS)` before line 140. Do not use `context.getGrantType()` here. `PermissionGrantType.process` reuses the same `Context` and delegates to this grant (PermissionGrantType.java:118-122), so that value would be the UMA grant.

findings.title: The base token-exchange path (V1, subject impersonation, external-token exchange) never records the grant, so those tokens are encoded with "na" instead of "te"
findings.description:
Only the `exchangeClientToOIDCClient` override in `StandardTokenExchangeProvider` sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` (StandardTokenExchangeProvider.java:237). The base implementation at lines 409-410 builds the token with `responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` and never sets the attribute. `exchangeClientToClient` (lines 288-299) dispatches to it, and it is reached from `V1TokenExchangeProvider.java:154`, `SubjectImpersonationTokenExchangeProvider.java:151`, and the external-token path (`AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:535`, reached from `V1TokenExchangeProvider.java:75` and `FederatedTokenExchangeProvider.java:68`). These exchanges get `na` in the token ID instead of `te` (`TokenExchangeGrantTypeFactory.getShortcut()`), so the same grant is tagged differently depending on which provider handled it.

Fix: set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` to `OAuth2Constants.TOKEN_EXCHANGE_GRANT_TYPE` in the base method before line 409. The override's own line can stay.

findings.title: UMA permission-grant RPTs are minted without recording the grant, so they are encoded with "na" instead of "pg"
findings.description:
After creating `clientSessionCtx` (line 350 or 352), `AuthorizationTokenService` builds the RPT with `tokenManager.responseBuilder(...).generateAccessToken()` at lines 357-358. Nothing sets `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` on that context, so `initToken` encodes the RPT with `na`. The RPT is produced by the UMA grant (`PermissionGrantType.java:187` calls `AuthorizationTokenService.instance().authorize`), and `PermissionGrantTypeFactory` declares shortcut "pg". This is the same gap as the two findings above, on a different path.

Fix: set `Constants.GRANT_TYPE` to `OAuth2Constants.UMA_GRANT_TYPE` on `clientSessionCtx` before line 357.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId inverts its grant check, so it returns false exactly when the expected grant shortcut matches
findings.description: `if (items[0].substring(3, 5).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` rejects a token ID when its grant matches and accepts it when it does not. The condition must be negated (`!...equals(...)`). Negating it alone would be wrong, though: because of the offset defect in the next finding, the check would then reject every correctly tagged token. The two fixes have to go together.

findings.title: isAccessTokenId reads the wrong characters, so its grant comparison never checks the grant
findings.description:
The encoder places the grant shortcut at 0-based characters 4-5. `DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:78-81` decodes it with `substring(4, 6)`, and `encodeTokenId` writes `sessionType + tokenType + grant + ':' + rawId` (lines 114-117). The matcher reads `substring(3, 5)`, which is the second character of the token-type shortcut plus the first character of the grant. The comment on line 482 ("4th char") counts from 1 and lands on index 3 as well. For a real token ID such as `onrtcc:<uuid>` (an authorization-code token tagged `cc`), `substring(3, 5)` is `"tc"`, which is not `"ac"`, so `isAccessTokenId("ac")` accepts it. The token-type second character is always `t` or `n`, so the matcher does not check the grant and verifies only the UUID shape.

Fix: use `substring(4, 6)` (together with the negation fix above).

findings.title: AccessTokenContext null-checks grantType twice and never checks rawTokenId
findings.description:
Line 73 is `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`, a copy of line 72 with the wrong variable. A null `rawTokenId` is accepted. `encodeTokenId` then concatenates it (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:117, `':' + getRawTokenId()`), yielding a token ID ending in `:null` with no error. No current caller passes null (TokenManager.java:1053 passes `KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()`), so the effect is latent.

Fix: `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed");`.

findings.title: Adding abstract getShortcut() to OAuth2GrantTypeFactory makes postInit fail for existing grant factories
findings.description:
`OAuth2GrantTypeFactory` gains `String getShortcut();` with no default (server-spi-private/.../OAuth2GrantTypeFactory.java:33). `postInit` (lines 70-76) calls `gtf.getShortcut()` on every registered `OAuth2GrantType` factory and puts the result into a `ConcurrentHashMap`. All nine in-repo factories implement it. An extension grant factory compiled against the previous SPI will either fail to compile against the new one, or throw `AbstractMethodError` at line 74 at runtime. That aborts `postInit` and therefore server startup. A `default` method returning null would not help: `grantsByShortcuts.put(null, ...)` throws NPE on line 75, and a grant with no shortcut would later fail in `encodeTokenId` (DefaultTokenContextEncoderProvider.java:110-112).

Fix: if the method stays abstract, document it as a breaking SPI change. Otherwise make it `default`, have `postInit` skip null shortcuts, and have `encodeTokenId` fall back to UNKNOWN instead of throwing.
